match.reason: None of the bank points compares buying an existing business with starting a new one; they cover start-up resources, the decision to start, market research, forces for change and marketing approaches.

draft.title: Buying a business or starting one
card: The owner takes over a business that already runs. Customers, staff and records come with it from the first day.
The owner builds the business from nothing. It usually costs less to begin, but it takes longer to win customers and build a team.
An existing business may carry old problems, such as a poor reputation, unhappy staff or debts. The buyer should check these before paying.
A buyer pays more up front for a business that already works. A new owner pays less up front but must wait for income to grow.
draft.remember: Buying gives a running business at a higher price. Starting new costs less but takes longer.

a.q: Which is a reason an owner might choose to buy an existing business rather than start a new one?
opts: It already has customers and records from day one
It usually costs less to begin than a new business
It cannot carry any problems from past owners
It lets the owner build the team from nothing
a.why: An existing business comes with customers, staff and records, so it can earn income straight away. The lower cost belongs to starting new, because buyers usually pay more up front.
a.clue: Think about what the buyer gets on the first day.

b.q: Jas wants to open a bakery in Bendigo and has limited savings. Another bakery is for sale, but locals say its service has been poor. Which statement best describes her choice?
opts: Starting new costs less but she must build up customers
Buying costs less and avoids any wait for customers
Starting new gives her staff and records at once
Buying is risk free because the bakery already trades
b.why: Jas has limited savings, and starting new usually costs less to begin. The cost is time, because she must win customers herself. Buying would bring customers at once but may carry the old problem of poor service, so it is not risk free.
b.clue: Which choice costs less to begin, and what does it cost in time?

a.best: It already has customers and records from day one

b.best: Starting new costs less but she must build up customers

problems.detail: The card says starting new 'usually' costs less to begin, but the remember line says 'Starting new costs less' with no qualifier. It states as a rule what the card gives only as a general tendency.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the explanations match the card. The only issue is minor: the remember line drops the card's 'usually', so starting new sounds like it always costs less.
